title: Use of a hemofilter to stabilize electrolyte balance and hemoglobin levels after application of Brettschneider cardioplegia
summary:
The application of cardioplegic solutions is essential for inducing controlled cardiac arrest (cardioplegia) to facilitate surgical interventions on the heart. However, this process is associated with potential pathophysiological alterations, most notably significant electrolyte shifts (e.g., sodium imbalances) and hemodilution, which leads to a decreased erythrocyte concentration.

This study investigates whether the integration of hemofiltration into the heart-lung machine (HLM) circuit can effectively counteract these adverse effects. The patient cohort is divided into two groups: Study Group A (utilizing a hemofilter) and Control Group B (without a hemofilter). Evaluation of the primary parameters is conducted by comparing laboratory data obtained from serial blood gas analyses (BGA).
conditions: Screening for hyponatremia, delirium, and anemia in cardiac surgery procedures
Delirium, not induced by alcohol and other psychoactive substances

interventions.name: Intervention group: After application of Brettschneider cardioplegia, patients receive hemofiltration with the DHF 02 hemofilter from LivaNova®.
Control group: Patients receive standard treatment without hemofiltration.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Surgery with cardioplegic Brettschneider solution
- Patients who are capable of giving consent and are over 18 years of age
- Elective cardiac bypass surgery with CPB
- HB above 9 g/dl at the start of surgery
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria:
- Refusal of study inclusion by the patient
- Emergency surgery
- Use of other cardioplegic solutions, such as Calafiore blood cardioplegia
- Bicaval cannulation
